data.name: Ekaant
data.gender_notes: Ekaant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'eka' meaning 'one' and 'ant' meaning 'end', 'Ekaant' symbolizes being in a state of solitude or aloneness, often with a deeper spiritual meaning. In Hindu mythology, it is the name of a sage who attained enlightenment through deep meditation and seclusion. The name Ekaant carries the meaning “Alone, Secluded” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ekaant usually hope their child will grow to embody alone, secluded and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the pursuit of inner peace and wisdom through solitude and self-reflection.
data.etymology: Ekaant belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Alone, Secluded.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ekaant total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: The sage Ekaant, also known as Ekantabhagavat or Ekantaranyaka, was an important figure in the 13th century Bhakti movement in India. He is said to have lived during the medieval period and was a prominent disciple of the legendary sage Ramanuja. Ekaant is known for his devotion to Lord Vishnu and his teachings on the importance of self-realization and the attainment of God.
